name: Ibn Az-Zubair
title: Meccan Companion & Scribe of the Uthmanic Committee
biography: Son of Az-Zubair bin Al-Awwam and Asma' bint Abi Bakr, nephew of Aisha, and one of the three Qurayshi members appointed by Caliph Uthman to copy the official codices alongside Zaid bin Thabit. Despite his role on Uthman's committee, classical reports in Tafsir al-Tabari and Sahih al-Bukhari record his preservation of select Companion readings in Mecca alongside Ibn Abbas, such as 'in the seasons of Hajj' (fi mawāsimi l-hajj) in Surah 2:198.

virtues.hadith_arabic: فَأَمَرَ عُثْمَانُ زَيْدَ بْنَ ثَابِتٍ وَعَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ وَسَعِيدَ بْنَ الْعَاصِ وَعَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ فَنَسَخُوهَا فِي الْمَصَاحِفِ
virtues.hadith_english: Uthman ordered Zaid bin Thabit, Abdullah bin Az-Zubair, Sa'id bin Al-As, and Abdur-Rahman bin Harith bin Hisham, and they copied the manuscripts into the Mushafs.

bio_text: Son of Az-Zubair bin Al-Awwam and Asma' bint Abi Bakr, nephew of Aisha, and one of the three Qurayshi members appointed by Caliph Uthman to copy the official codices alongside Zaid bin Thabit. Despite his role on Uthman's committee, classical reports in Tafsir al-Tabari and Sahih al-Bukhari record his preservation of select Companion readings in Mecca alongside Ibn Abbas, such as 'in the seasons of Hajj' (fi mawāsimi l-hajj) in Surah 2:198.

variants.short_title: Ibn Abbas Adds 'During the Pilgrimage Seasons' (2:198)
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran says 'There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord.' Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr recited an extra phrase at the end: 'during the seasons of the Hajj pilgrimage.'
variants.title: Addition of 'Fi Mawasimi l-Hajj' in Q. 2:198 (Ibn Abbas & Ibn al-Zubayr)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari (1770, 2050, 2098, 4519), Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Abbas (as well as 'Abdullah bin al-Zubayr and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud) recited Q. 2:198 with the added prepositional phrase 'فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ' ('during the seasons of the pilgrimage'): 'لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ'. Ibn 'Abbas stated that the verse was revealed with these exact words when early Muslims hesitated to conduct trade at the seasonal markets of 'Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu al-Majaz during the Hajj.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord.
variants.variant_target_arabic: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ
variants.variant_target_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of the pilgrimage.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord. When you press on from ‘Arafāt, remember God at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before you were indeed among those who had gone astray.
variants.variant_full_arabic: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
variants.variant_full_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of the pilgrimage. When you press on from ‘Arafāt, remember God at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before you were indeed among those who had gone astray.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars classify 'fi mawasimi l-hajj' as an explanatory gloss (qira'ah tafsiriyyah) specifying the time when seeking commercial bounty was questioned, or a phrase whose recitation was abrogated.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 2050 and 4519, Ibn 'Abbas explicitly states 'thus the verse was revealed' (fa-nazalat: 'fi mawasimi l-hajj') and continued reciting it that way after the Uthmanic standardization, as did Caliph 'Abdullah bin al-Zubayr in Mecca.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمِجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ فَكَأَنَّهُمْ تَأَثَّمُوا فِيهِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were marketplaces in the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance. When Islam came, Muslims felt that marketing there might be a sin. So, the Divine Inspiration came: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمَجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ تَأَثَّمُوا مِنَ التِّجَارَةِ فِيهَا، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ كَذَا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were markets in the Pre-Islamic period. When the people embraced Islam they considered it a sin to trade there. So, the following Holy Verse came:-- 'There is no harm for you if you seek of the bounty of your Lord (Allah) in the Hajj season." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited it like this
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ كَذَا
hadiths.highlight_english: 'There is no harm for you if you seek of the bounty of your Lord (Allah) in the Hajj season." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited it like this

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمَجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَتَأَثَّمُوا أَنْ يَتَّجِرُوا فِي الْمَوَاسِمِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Mijanna and Dhul-Majaz were markets during the Pre-islamic Period. They (i.e. Muslims) considered it a sin to trade there during the Hajj time (i.e. season), so this Verse was revealed:-- "There is no harm for you if you seek of the Bounty of your Lord during the Hajj season
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ
hadiths.highlight_english: so this Verse was revealed:-- "There is no harm for you if you seek of the Bounty of your Lord during the Hajj season

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt:
3768 - حدثت عن أبي هشام الرفاعي، قال: حدثنا وكيع، عن طلحة بن عمرو، عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج ".
3778 - حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى، قال: أخبرنا عبد الرزاق، قال: أخبرنا ابن عيينة، عن عبيد الله بن أبي يزيد، قال: سمعت ابن الزبير يقرأ: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt:
3768 - It was narrated from Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, from Waki', from Talhah bin 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: "There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
3778 - Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us... from 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr recite: "There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال وكيع : حدثنا طلحة بن عمرو الحضرمي ، عن عطاء ، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج " . [ وقال عبد الرزاق : عن أبيه عيينة ، عن عبيد الله بن أبي يزيد : سمعت ابن الزبير يقول : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج " ] .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Waki' reported that Talhah bin 'Amr Al-Hadrami narrated from 'Ata' that Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj." 'Abdur-Razzaq reported from his father, from 'Uyaynah, from 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Yazid: I heard Ibn Az-Zubayr say: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."

variants.short_title: The Lost Verse of the Two Valleys of Gold
variants.plain_english_hook: Ubayy bin Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, and Anas bin Malik testified in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim that the 'Two Valleys of Gold' passage was recited as Quranic revelation before being omitted from the Mushaf.
variants.title: The Son of Adam and Two Valleys of Gold Passage Attested by Ubayy bin Ka'b
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari (6437, 6438, 6440) and Sahih Muslim (1048b, 1049), Ubayy bin Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, Anas bin Malik, and Ibn Az-Zubair report the prophetic recitation: 'If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would desire a second, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust, and Allah turns in mercy to whoever repents.' Ubayy bin Ka'b states that the Companions considered this passage part of the Quran until Surah At-Takathur (102:1) was revealed, while Ibn Abbas and Anas bin Malik express uncertainty over whether it was revealed as Quran or prophetic speech.
variants.variant_target_arabic: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَادِيَانِ، وَلَنْ يَمْلَأَ فَاهُ إِلَّا التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
variants.variant_target_english: If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would love to have two valleys, and nothing fills his mouth except dust, and Allah forgives whoever repents to Him.
variants.variant_full_arabic: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَادِيَانِ، وَلَنْ يَمْلَأَ فَاهُ إِلَّا التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
variants.variant_full_english: If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would love to have two valleys, and nothing fills his mouth except dust, and Allah forgives whoever repents to Him.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators such as Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari explain that this passage was either an abrogated Quranic verse whose recitation was lifted after Surah At-Takathur (102:1) was revealed, or a Hadith Qudsi that some Companions initially mistook for Quran.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6437 and Sahih Muslim 1048b, senior authorities such as Ibn Abbas and Anas bin Malik explicitly state, 'I do not know whether it is from the Quran or not,' while Ubayy bin Ka'b and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (Muslim 1050) affirm that it was recited as part of a Quranic surah.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَخْلَدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَطَاءً، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ مِثْلَ وَادٍ مَالاً لأَحَبَّ أَنَّ لَهُ إِلَيْهِ مِثْلَهُ، وَلاَ يَمْلأُ عَيْنَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If the son of Adam had money equal to a valley, then he will wish for another similar to it, for nothing can satisfy the eye of Adam's son except dust. And Allah forgives him who repents to Him." Ibn `Abbas said: I do not know whether this saying was quoted from the Qur'an or not. `Ata' said, "I heard Ibn Az-Zubair saying this narration while he was on the pulpit
hadiths.highlight_arabic: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ
hadiths.highlight_english: Ibn `Abbas said: I do not know whether this saying was quoted from the Qur'an or not.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَقَالَ لَنَا أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، عَنْ أُبَىٍّ، قَالَ كُنَّا نَرَى هَذَا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ‏}‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Ubayy said (referring to the hadith above), "We considered this as a saying from the Qur'an till the Surah (beginning with):"The mutual rivalry (for piling up of worldly things) diverts you' (102:1) was revealed"
hadiths.highlight_arabic: عَنْ أُبَىٍّ، قَالَ كُنَّا نَرَى هَذَا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ‏}
hadiths.highlight_english: We considered this as a saying from the Qur'an till the Surah (beginning with):"The mutual rivalry (for piling up of worldly things) diverts you' (102:1) was revealed

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى، وَسَعِيدُ بْنُ مَنْصُورٍ، وَقُتَيْبَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، قَالَ يَحْيَى أَخْبَرَنَا وَقَالَ الآخَرَانِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَوَانَةَ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَوْ كَانَ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَانِ مِنْ مَالٍ لاَبْتَغَى وَادِيًا ثَالِثًا وَلاَ يَمْلأُ جَوْفَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، وَابْنُ، بَشَّارٍ قَالَ ابْنُ الْمُثَنَّى حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا شُعْبَةُ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ قَتَادَةَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ - فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَشَىْءٌ أُنْزِلَ أَمْ شَىْءٌ كَانَ يَقُولُهُ - بِمِثْلِ حَدِيثِ أَبِي عَوَانَةَ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Anas reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: 'If the son of Adam were to possess two valleys of riches, he would long for the third one. And the stomach of the son of Adam is not filled but with dust. And Allah returns to him who repents.' And Anas b. Malik reported: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying this — and I do not know whether it was something revealed or something he used to say — similar to the hadith of Abu 'Awanah.
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَشَىْءٌ أُنْزِلَ أَمْ شَىْءٌ كَانَ يَقُولُهُ
hadiths.highlight_english: I do not know whether it was something revealed or something he used to say

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنِي زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، وَهَارُونُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَطَاءً، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ مِلْءَ وَادٍ مَالاً لأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ إِلَيْهِ مِثْلُهُ وَلاَ يَمْلأُ نَفْسَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ وَاللَّهُ يَتُوبُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ زُهَيْرٍ قَالَ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ‏.‏ لَمْ يَذْكُرِ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Ibn Abbas reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:If there were for the son of Adam a valley full of riches, he would long to possess another one like it. and Ibn Adam does not feel satiated but with dust. And Allah returns to him who returns (to Him). Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an or not; and in the narration transmitted by Zuhair it was said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an, and he made no mention of Ibn Abbas
hadiths.highlight_arabic: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ
hadiths.highlight_english: Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an or not

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا محمد بن خلف العسقلاني، قال: ثنا آدم، قال: ثنا حماد بن سلمة، عن ثابت البناني، عن أنس بن مالك، عن أُبيّ بن كعب، قال: كنا نرى أن هذا الحديث من القرآن: " لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال، لتمنى واديا ثالثا، ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب، ثم يتوب الله على من تاب " حتى نـزلت هذه السورة: ( أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ ) إلى آخرها.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Muhammad bin Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, from Adam, from Hammad bin Salamah, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas bin Malik, from Ubayy bin Ka'b, who said: "We used to think that this statement was from the Qur'an: 'If the Son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would desire a third valley; and nothing fills the belly of the Son of Adam except dust, then Allah turns in forgiveness to whomever repents,' until this Surah was revealed: {Rivalry diverts you,} to its end."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: كنا نرى أن هذا الحديث من القرآن: " لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال، لتمنى واديا ثالثا
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: We used to think that this statement was from the Qur'an: 'If the Son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would desire a third valley

variants.variant_arabic: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَادِيَانِ، وَلَنْ يَمْلَأَ فَاهُ إِلَّا التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
variants.variant_english: If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would love to have two valleys, and nothing fills his mouth except dust, and Allah forgives whoever repents to Him.
variants.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَخْلَدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَطَاءً، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ مِثْلَ وَادٍ مَالاً لأَحَبَّ أَنَّ لَهُ إِلَيْهِ مِثْلَهُ، وَلاَ يَمْلأُ عَيْنَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If the son of Adam had money equal to a valley, then he will wish for another similar to it, for nothing can satisfy the eye of Adam's son except dust. And Allah forgives him who repents to Him." Ibn `Abbas said: I do not know whether this saying was quoted from the Qur'an or not. `Ata' said, "I heard Ibn Az-Zubair saying this narration while he was on the pulpit
